newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia FinMin says inflation target is in sight.
newsitem.headline: Colombia FinMin says inflation target is in sight.

text.p: Colombia's Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo said Wednesday that the 12-month inflation figure to the end of July would be 18 percent -- in line with the year- end target of 18 percent.

"There's no doubt in my mind that we will fulfill our inflation target this year," Ocampo said at a forum on macroeconomic targets in Bogota. He said that the 12-month inflation figure would be already down to 18 percent by the end of this month.

Colombian inflation for the 12 months to the end of June was running at 18.67 percent, down from 1996 inflation of 21.68 percent. Critics, however, say the fall in inflation has only be achieved at the cost of spiralling unemployment and economic recession.

Since it began setting economic targets in 1991, Colombia's central bank has never fulfilled its inflation target. But government officials and many independent analysts agree that the bank's forceast will be correct for 1997.
Mauricio Cardenas, head of the independent economic think- tank Fedesarrollo, was, however, less optimistic.

He forcast 1997 inflation would end between 18.8 percent and 19.2 percent. Cardenas went on to forecast inflation of 19.4 percent in 1998. The central bank has not yet issued predictions for next year.
